faq.q: Why is it so quiet after it snows?
faq.a: Fresh snow is full of air gaps that soak up sound instead of reflecting it, much like acoustic foam. Fewer people and cars moving about makes it quieter still.
asks: Why does snow make things silent?
Why does the world sound muffled in snow?

faq.a: Yes, fresh fluffy snow absorbs sound well. Sound waves get lost bouncing between the ice crystals and air pockets, and their energy turns to a tiny bit of heat.
asks: How does snow soak up noise?

faq.q: Why does old icy snow sound crunchy and loud?
faq.a: When snow melts and refreezes, the air gaps close up and it forms a hard crust. Hard surfaces reflect sound, so the quiet effect disappears, and stepping on it crunches.

faq.q: How much air is in fresh snow?
faq.a: Freshly fallen snow can be more than 90 percent air. That is what makes it light, fluffy and good at absorbing sound.
asks: Why is fresh snow so light?

faq.q: Why do recording studios have foam on the walls?
faq.a: Foam is full of tiny air pockets, like fresh snow. Sound enters and loses energy instead of bouncing back, so the room has fewer echoes.

facts: Freshly fallen snow can be more than 90 percent air.
Porous materials such as fresh snow and acoustic foam absorb sound, while hard, smooth surfaces reflect it.
